generatedProse.concept-context: In the School of Sport, the goals you set shape how much you get from a module. A performance goal fixes on one mark, such as a grade for a single case-study report. A mastery goal aims at a capability you will reuse across the course, such as assessing an injury or designing a rehabilitation programme. Turning a vague wish into a mastery goal is what keeps your learning moving forward. The same choice faces a sport management student planning a campaign or a coach building a season, not just a therapist.
generatedProse.worked-example:
Two sport therapy students set themselves a goal at the start of a new rehabilitation module.

Tom writes down a single aim: get at least 65 in the final case-study report. It is specific, but it is a performance goal fixed on one mark. When an early practical on joint assessment does not count towards that report, he puts little into it, and the goal gives him no steer on how to actually improve.

Amara starts with the same loose wish to do well, but rephrases it: get better at assessing an injury and justifying a rehab plan. That is a mastery goal, aimed at a capability rather than one mark. It guides every task on the module, counting or not, because each is a chance to practise the assessment the goal names.

Both students set a goal. Only Amara's goal moved her learning forward across the whole module.
generatedProse.summary: In the School of Sport, goals come in two kinds. Performance goals target a mark, while mastery goals build a capability, such as assessing an injury, that lasts beyond one report. A vague wish is neither until you make it specific. You can now tell the two apart, rephrase a loose aim into a mastery goal, and set one of your own. With mindset, motivation and goals all working, you are ready to keep progressing in the School of Sport.

check.body: In the worked example, what made Amara's goal move her learning forward where Tom's did not?

items.text: It aimed at a reusable capability, assessing an injury, so it guided every task on the module.
It set a higher target mark than Tom's goal.
It was written down more neatly.
It focused only on the final case-study report that counted.

feedback.correct: That's right. The mastery goal aimed at a capability, so it guided every task, counting or not.
feedback.incorrectNotFinal: Not quite. Look for what let Amara's goal guide work across the whole module.
feedback.incorrectFinal: Amara's goal moved learning forward because it aimed at a reusable capability and guided every task. The others stay fixed on a single mark.
